question: What happens to prohibition when viewed from the nondual path?
premises: From another standpoint, all this may appear prohibited.
A prohibition is meaningful only when clearly demonstrated.
One who rests on the nondual path sees beyond fixed oppositions.
inference: Therefore, once prohibition is shown in that limited way, its force is questioned for one established on the nondual path.
plain_english: And all this is prohibited only from that other standpoint; for when its prohibition is clearly shown, what force does it have for one who rests on the nondual path?
